partner_context.their_ambition: The Maharashtra Maritime Board is the State authority for ports and water transport in Maharashtra, developing Mumbai's passenger water-transport network — the Gateway–Mandwa RoPax, the Belapur water taxi, Elephanta and historic harbour ferries, plus a planned Mumbai water-metro — to relieve one of the world's most congested cities.
partner_context.their_pressure: Mumbai's harbour ferries and the new water taxis still run on diesel, even as the MMB pushes new passenger water transport to relieve the city's gridlock — leaving a clear opening for zero-emission vessels. Growth and the net-zero mandate both demand fleet renewal without disturbing the services people rely on today.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission foiling layer for the network the Maharashtra Maritime Board is already building out — turning multi-hour road commutes between South Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and the Alibaug coast into fast, clean water lines.

objections.concern: Does this compete with the existing public ferry service?
objections.response: No — Navier is a passenger-only foiling layer above the existing service, adding fast frequencies on the busy corridors the conventional boats can't run economically. It complements the electrification already underway.
Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at existing piers — no new shore power, vertiports or rights-of-way.

objections.concern: Is foiling safe in busy, shared public waterways?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil and low-wake zones near piers, ferry lanes and moorings, automatic speed and wake limits in shared water, and conventional low-speed handling everywhere it isn't cleared to fly.

close.title: A zero-emission water layer that grows with the city.
close.body: Start on the busiest corridors, scale across the full network, then mature the service — a zero-emission foiling tier that advances the authority's net-zero mandate while the services people rely on keep running underneath.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — the open water and the piers already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the long-range hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the charging excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
